title: FastAPI Web APIs
description: Beginner-to-advanced FastAPI reference covering routing, validation, Pydantic, dependency injection, async execution, authentication, authorization, errors, middleware, lifespan, databases, background tasks, WebSockets, testing, OpenAPI, security, performance, and deployment.

sections.title: Application, Routing & Parameters
sections.description: Define typed HTTP contracts and keep transport logic thin.

subtopics.title: FastAPI App & Path Operations
subtopics.description: Path-operation decorators bind an HTTP method/path to a callable; annotations drive parsing, validation, OpenAPI, and editor support.

callouts.title: Route Order Can Matter
callouts.text: Declare fixed routes such as /users/me before /users/{user_id} when both can match. Use typed path converters/validation to reduce ambiguity.

subtopics.title: Path, Query, Header & Cookie Parameters
subtopics.description: Use Annotated with Path/Query/Header/Cookie for constraints, aliases, metadata, deprecation, and repeated values.

codeBlocks.code:
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Header, Path, Query

@app.get('/items/{item_id}')
async def list_related(
    item_id: Annotated[int, Path(gt=0)],
    q: Annotated[str | None, Query(min_length=2, max_length=100)] = None,
    tags: Annotated[list[str], Query()] = [],
    request_id: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias='X-Request-ID')] = None,
): ...

callouts.title: Validation Is Not Authorization
callouts.text: A valid item_id may still belong to another tenant. Verify authenticated access to the resource in the service/data boundary.

subtopics.title: APIRouter, Prefixes & Project Structure
subtopics.description: Compose routers by bounded API/domain area with shared prefixes, tags, dependencies, and responses; avoid one giant route module.

callouts.title: Routes Translate; Services Decide
callouts.text: Keep HTTP extraction/status/response in routes, business policy in services/domain, and persistence details in repositories. This enables unit tests without ASGI.

sections.title: Pydantic Models & API Contracts
sections.description: Separate request, domain, persistence, and response representations where their trust and evolution differ.

subtopics.title: BaseModel, Fields & Validators
subtopics.description: Pydantic parses/validates boundary data into typed models. Field constraints describe local values; model validators enforce cross-field invariants.

callouts.title: Forbid Unknown Write Fields
callouts.text: extra='forbid' catches client mistakes and prevents mass-assignment surprises. Add fields deliberately through API evolution.

subtopics.title: Create, Update & Read Models
subtopics.description: Use distinct write/read models so clients cannot set server-controlled fields and responses cannot accidentally expose internal secrets.

callouts.title: Response Model Is a Security Filter
callouts.text: Always define/output explicit safe fields. Never return ORM/domain objects containing password hashes, tokens, internal flags, or tenant-private relationships by convenience.

subtopics.title: Serialization, Aliases & API Evolution
subtopics.description: Configure external naming and serialization without contaminating domain names; version breaking contracts and add compatible optional fields carefully.

callouts.title: JSON Numeric/Time Semantics
callouts.text: Define Decimal, datetime/timezone, UUID, enum, null, and large integer representation in the public contract and consumer tests.

sections.title: Dependency Injection & Lifespan
sections.description: Use dependency graphs for request-scoped resources, policy, and replaceable adapters without hiding domain logic.

subtopics.title: Depends, Annotated & Sub-Dependencies
subtopics.description: A dependency callable can declare its own dependencies; FastAPI resolves/caches the graph per request by default and integrates requirements into OpenAPI.

callouts.title: Dependency Graph Can Hide Work
callouts.text: Keep dependencies focused and observable. Deep graphs that perform unrelated database/network operations make latency, transaction ownership, and testing hard to understand.

subtopics.title: Dependencies with yield
subtopics.description: Yield dependencies acquire a request resource, provide it to downstream dependencies/handler, and clean up afterward—even on exceptions.

codeBlocks.code:
async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with session_factory() as session:
        try:
            yield session
            await session.commit()
        except BaseException:
            await session.rollback()
            raise

SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]

callouts.title: Define Transaction Boundaries Deliberately
callouts.text: Automatic commit after every request may be wrong for streaming responses, partial work, or multiple use cases. Prefer explicit unit-of-work semantics and test rollback/cancellation.

subtopics.title: Application Lifespan & Shared Resources
subtopics.description: Use lifespan for process-level initialization/cleanup such as pools, clients, models, and telemetry; store handles in app state or explicit containers.

codeBlocks.code:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.http = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=5)
    app.state.pool = await create_pool()
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        await app.state.http.aclose()
        await app.state.pool.close()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

callouts.title: Every Worker Has Its Own Lifespan
callouts.text: In-memory state/pools/models are per process. Coordinate migrations, singleton jobs, rate limits, and shared state through external systems or deployment jobs.

sections.title: Async Execution, Databases & Background Work
sections.description: Match function type and workload so blocking operations do not stall the event loop.

subtopics.title: async def vs def
subtopics.description: Use async def when calling awaitable libraries; FastAPI runs normal def path/dependencies in a thread pool. Blocking calls inside async def block the event loop.

table.title: FastAPI Handler Execution Model
rows: Async database, HTTP, queue, and file APIs
Runs on the event loop and yields at await
FastAPI runs it in a worker thread pool
Mostly async work with an isolated blocking call
Explicitly moves blocking work off the event loop
Cancellation may not stop the underlying blocking operation
Requires queueing, idempotency, retries, and job status

callouts.title: async Does Not Make CPU Work Parallel
callouts.text: Image processing, ML inference, compression, or large serialization blocks the worker unless moved to processes/native workers or external jobs.

subtopics.title: Database Sessions, Repositories & Pagination
subtopics.description: Create request/unit-of-work sessions, parameterize queries, avoid lazy-loading during serialization, and paginate bounded responses with stable ordering.

callouts.title: Avoid N+1 and Unbounded Lists
callouts.text: Select required relations/columns explicitly, cap page sizes, use stable cursor keys, and measure query count/latency. response_model cannot fix inefficient fetching.

subtopics.title: BackgroundTasks vs Durable Queues
subtopics.description: BackgroundTasks runs small in-process work after sending the response. Durable, retryable, scheduled, long, CPU-heavy, or cross-instance work belongs in a queue/worker system.

callouts.title: BackgroundTasks Dies with the Process
callouts.text: It provides no durable delivery, distributed coordination, retry policy, or status. Do not use it for payments, required emails, exports, or important jobs.

sections.title: Authentication, Authorization & Security
sections.description: Use standards-based identity while enforcing resource-level policy on every operation.

subtopics.title: OAuth2/Bearer Identity Dependencies
subtopics.description: FastAPI security utilities describe schemes in OpenAPI and extract credentials; your code must validate issuer, audience, signature, expiry, claims, and user/session state.

codeBlocks.code:
oauth2 = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl='/v1/auth/token')

async def current_user(token: Annotated[str, Security(oauth2)]) -> User:
    claims = verifier.verify(token, issuer=ISSUER, audience=AUDIENCE)
    user = await users.find_active(claims.subject)
    if not user: raise HTTPException(401, 'invalid credentials', headers={'WWW-Authenticate': 'Bearer'})
    return user

callouts.title: Do Not Invent Token Cryptography
callouts.text: Use a maintained identity provider/library and key rotation. Never trust unverified JWT claims or select algorithms from attacker-controlled headers without policy.

subtopics.title: Scopes, Roles & Resource Authorization
subtopics.description: Authentication answers who; authorization answers whether this principal may perform this action on this resource/tenant now.

codeBlocks.code:
async def editable_order(
    order_id: UUID,
    user: CurrentUserDep,
    repository: OrderRepositoryDep,
) -> Order:
    order = await repository.get(order_id)
    if order.tenant_id != user.tenant_id or not user.can('orders:write'):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)  # avoid cross-tenant existence leak
    return order

callouts.title: Dependency Reuse Helps Consistency
callouts.text: Create focused policy dependencies for repeated rules, but keep authoritative checks near data mutation so alternate entry points cannot bypass them.

subtopics.title: CORS, CSRF, Trusted Hosts & Limits
subtopics.description: CORS controls browsers, not server authorization. Cookie credentials require CSRF defense; proxy/host/origin/body/rate/time limits belong in an end-to-end deployment policy.

codeBlocks.code:
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=['https://app.example.com'],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=['GET', 'POST', 'PATCH'],
    allow_headers=['Authorization', 'Content-Type', 'X-CSRF-Token'],
)
app.add_middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=['api.example.com'])

callouts.title: Wildcard Credentials Are Unsafe/Invalid
callouts.text: Use exact origins when credentials are allowed. Enforce HTTPS, secure cookie attributes, CSRF tokens/origin checks, request limits, and proxy-header trust at known hops.

sections.title: Responses, Errors & Middleware
sections.description: Return stable public errors and use middleware only for true cross-cutting request concerns.

subtopics.title: Status Codes, Headers, Files & Streaming
subtopics.description: Use response_model for data contracts and specialized responses for redirects, files, streams, and no-content behavior; set correct media/cache/content-disposition headers.

callouts.title: Streaming Holds Resources
callouts.text: Handle disconnect/cancellation, close generators/files, avoid holding database transactions for long streams, and ensure proxies do not buffer unexpectedly.

subtopics.title: HTTPException & Global Exception Mapping
subtopics.description: Raise HTTPException for transport-level expected failures or map domain exceptions centrally into a consistent safe error envelope.

callouts.title: Do Not Leak Internal Exceptions
callouts.text: Log stack/context server-side with correlation ID, but return stable messages/codes. Avoid SQL, paths, tokens, stack traces, or cross-tenant existence details.

subtopics.title: Middleware, Request IDs & Timing
subtopics.description: Middleware wraps the ASGI app; ordering is nested and affects errors, CORS, compression, sessions, logging, and timing. Prefer pure ASGI middleware for advanced streaming/context behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
@app.middleware('http')
async def request_context(request: Request, call_next):
    request.state.request_id = request.headers.get('x-request-id') or str(uuid4())
    started = monotonic()
    try:
        response = await call_next(request)
    finally:
        metrics.observe('http_duration', monotonic() - started)
    response.headers['x-request-id'] = request.state.request_id
    return response

callouts.title: Cardinality and Personal Data
callouts.text: Do not use raw paths, user IDs, tokens, request bodies, or arbitrary error text as metric labels/log fields. Normalize routes and apply privacy/redaction policy.

sections.title: WebSockets, OpenAPI & Testing
sections.description: Treat long-lived connections and generated API descriptions as production contracts.

subtopics.title: WebSockets & Connection Management
subtopics.description: Accept, authenticate, receive/send, handle disconnect, bound queues/message sizes, heartbeat, and cleanup. Multi-worker broadcast requires external pub/sub.

codeBlocks.code:
@app.websocket('/ws/updates')
async def updates(socket: WebSocket):
    user = await authenticate_websocket(socket)
    await socket.accept()
    subscription = await broker.subscribe(user.tenant_id)
    try:
        async for event in subscription:
            await socket.send_json(event.to_public_dict())
    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        pass
    finally:
        await subscription.close()

callouts.title: Backpressure and Slow Clients
callouts.text: A slow client can grow memory indefinitely. Bound per-connection queues, define drop/disconnect policy, limit message rate/size, and monitor active connections.

subtopics.title: OpenAPI, Documentation & SDK Contracts
subtopics.description: Operation IDs, tags, summaries, examples, response models, security requirements, and deprecations shape generated docs and clients.

codeBlocks.code:
@router.post(
    '',
    operation_id='createOrder',
    response_model=OrderRead,
    status_code=201,
    responses={409: {'model': ErrorResponse, 'description': 'Order conflict'}},
    summary='Create an order',
)
async def create_order(...): ...

callouts.title: Schema Diff in CI
callouts.text: Export OpenAPI, lint it, detect breaking changes, and run consumer/contract tests. Generated docs are not a substitute for semantic guarantees and examples.

subtopics.title: TestClient, Async Tests & Dependency Overrides
subtopics.description: Test services/domain directly; use TestClient for synchronous API tests or HTTPX ASGI transport for async integration; override dependencies with fakes and reset afterward.

codeBlocks.code:
def test_create_order(client: TestClient, fake_service: FakeOrderService):
    app.dependency_overrides[get_order_service] = lambda: fake_service
    try:
        response = client.post('/v1/orders', json={'sku': 'ABC-1', 'quantity': 2})
        assert response.status_code == 201
        assert response.json()['sku'] == 'ABC-1'
    finally:
        app.dependency_overrides.clear()

callouts.title: Run Lifespan in Tests
callouts.text: Use TestClient as a context manager or an explicit lifespan manager when startup resources/events matter. Isolate databases and avoid live network/time.

sections.title: Deployment, Observability & Performance
sections.description: Operate ASGI workers with correct proxy, lifecycle, capacity, and telemetry behavior.

subtopics.title: ASGI Server, Workers & Graceful Shutdown
subtopics.description: Run with a production ASGI server, configure trusted proxy headers, concurrency/backlog/keep-alive/grace timeouts, and choose worker count from measured CPU/memory/workload.

codeBlocks.code:
fastapi run app/main.py --port 8000 --proxy-headers
# or deployment-approved ASGI command with explicit workers/timeouts

# Development only:
fastapi dev app/main.py

callouts.title: Do Not Multiply Workers Blindly
callouts.text: Each process duplicates memory, pools, caches, and startup work. In Kubernetes, balance workers per Pod versus Pod replicas and downstream connection limits.

subtopics.title: Containers, Migrations & Health
subtopics.description: Build one immutable image, run non-root, execute migrations as a coordinated deployment job, and expose lightweight distinct liveness/readiness endpoints.

codeBlocks.code:
Liveness: event loop/process can respond; avoid dependency fan-out
Readiness: instance can accept traffic; include critical local initialization
Startup: slow model/config warmup completed
Migration: one controlled job, backward-compatible expand/contract
Shutdown: stop intake, cancel/drain work, close pools/clients within grace

callouts.title: Never Run Uncoordinated Migrations in Every Worker
callouts.text: Concurrent startup migrations race, delay readiness, and complicate rollback. Use a deployment job/lock and schema compatible with mixed app versions.

subtopics.title: Logs, Metrics, Traces & Capacity
subtopics.description: Measure route-normalized request rate, latency, errors, saturation, event-loop/thread-pool behavior, database/upstream pools, queue depth, payload size, and worker memory.

codeBlocks.code:
Logs: request ID/trace ID, route, status, duration; redact secrets/PII
Metrics: RED + pool/queue/event-loop/worker resource signals
Traces: inbound → dependencies → database/queue
Load test: realistic payloads, auth, DB, failure, keep-alive, slow clients
Profile: serialization/validation, queries, CPU, memory—not only framework overhead

callouts.title: Tail Latency and Saturation
callouts.text: Average response time hides overload. Track p95/p99, timeouts, pool waits, rejected work, and recovery after spikes; enforce concurrency/backpressure.

sections.title: Production Readiness Checklist
sections.description: Review API contract, trust, ownership, async behavior, data, resilience, and deployment together.

subtopics.title: API & Operations Checklist
subtopics.description: A typed route is only one layer of a secure reliable API.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Routes are thin and public request/response models are separate
□ Unknown write fields, sizes, formats, and pagination are bounded
□ Responses expose only explicit safe fields
□ Every operation authenticates/authorizes resource and tenant
□ Token issuer/audience/signature/expiry and rotation are verified
□ Cookie APIs have CSRF defense; CORS/host/proxy trust is exact
□ async routes call no blocking libraries or CPU-heavy work
□ Sessions/transactions/resources have clear ownership and cleanup
□ Database queries avoid N+1 and unbounded results
□ Important background work uses a durable queue
□ Errors are stable safe envelopes with correlation IDs
□ Streaming/WebSockets bound queues, sizes, time, and disconnect cleanup
□ OpenAPI is linted/diffed and contracts are tested
□ Lifespan and dependency overrides are exercised in tests
□ Worker/Pod/pool/concurrency settings derive from load tests
□ Migrations are coordinated and compatible with rolling versions
□ Health, graceful shutdown, logs, metrics, traces, and alerts are proven

callouts.title: Framework Convenience Does Not Replace System Design
callouts.text: Automatic validation, DI, and OpenAPI reduce plumbing. They do not provide authorization, transaction correctness, durability, backpressure, capacity planning, secret management, or safe deployment automatically.
